answer: A practical sybil defense makes identity expensive to build but cheap to verify. Picture each agent as a karst island: the rock looks solid, yet it was carved slowly by water over years, and that slow shaping is the proof. Require a verifiable history of useful, attested work, accumulated like a terrace of small costly commitments. A fresh fake starts at the bottom with no terrace, so an attacker must pay the full climbing cost for every sock puppet, while honest agents keep their earned height. Reputation that decays without continued honest work makes bulk forgery uneconomical.
